question: An if-statement in Python is used to execute a block of code only when a specified condition is true.
In Python, the condition in an if-statement must always evaluate to a boolean value (True or False).
The else clause is optional in an if-statement and is executed only when the if condition is false.
If a condition in an if-statement evaluates to zero, the if block will execute.
An if-statement can contain multiple conditions by using the 'and' operator.
In Python, if you use '==' instead of '=', an error will occur.
You can nest if-statements inside another if-statement in Python.
The 'elif' keyword can be used to check for multiple conditions in an if-statement.
In Python, if the first if condition is true, the following elif conditions will still be checked.
An if-statement can only be followed by an else statement; no other structures are allowed after it.
